title: Reconstruction Atlas
tagline: How the Bible is now, how it has been, and the earliest form we can still recover.

passages.title: The allotment of the nations
passages.hook: The Most High divides the nations by Israel’s census — or by the number of the sons of God.

passages.title: Let all the gods worship him
passages.hook: Hebrews quotes a line most Protestant Old Testaments no longer print.

passages.title: Two books of Jeremiah
passages.hook: Greek Jeremiah is about an eighth shorter, with a different chapter order. Two editions circulated.

passages.title: Two beginnings
passages.hook: A seven-day cosmos and a garden tale stand side by side, not as a copyist error.

passages.title: Pierced, or like a lion
passages.hook: One letter decides whether the verse reads as crucifixion or as a lion at the hands.

passages.title: The ending that grew
passages.hook: The oldest Greek copies of Mark stop at 16:8. Later Bibles keep going.

passages.title: A book that left the canon
passages.hook: Jude quotes Enoch as prophecy. Qumran copied it. Ethiopia kept it. Most Bibles did not.
